generatedBy: scripts/landmarks/landmark-targets-next.ts --kit-open --monument-types=church,school,almshouse,mansion,warehouse,workshop,coachHouse --exclude=docs/reports/landmark-targets-20261115.json (raw list docs/reports/landmark-targets-20261120-raw.json), BAG addresses, landmark-brief contact sheets read by hand (artifacts/landmark-briefs/<id>/contact.jpg)
method: Candidates: OSM buildings and POIs with wikidata/wikipedia/historic/tourism/civic, religious and cultural amenity or building tags, plus register pands (monument-facts.json) of the types church, school, almshouse, mansion, warehouse, workshop and coachHouse. Pands under a bespoke model, a covers.json bespoke install, a catalogue suppress entry or a 20261115 verdict are out; ordinary/chunk/recipe kit installs stay in, as drawnAs=kit. Score = ride exposure (ride-visibility/v1) x recognisability (Wikipedia 2, wikidata 1.4, monument 1.2) x misrepresentation (generic 1.0, kit 0.7), within 2.6 km of the Dam. The curated order then reads the photos: civic, religious and cultural buildings first, then buildings that a generic block misrepresents badly, then evidence (a clear, square panorama of the main front).
ride: ride-visibility/v1: teachable destinations ≤ 6 km of the Dam, seeded pairs 1–6 km, bike graph shortest paths, 5 m samples, walls ≥ 2 m within 60 m on their outer side with a 2D footprint sightline; score = Σ sample m × passes × visible facing-wall m

targets.name: Hotel De Roode Leeuw (Damrak 93-94, 1911, Foeke Kuipers)
targets.reason: On the Damrak, the busiest ride in the game, 70 m from the Dam. Gemeentelijk monument 210017 and a Wikipedia article. Five-bay hotel front with a big arched first-floor arcade, balconies, a dormer roof and the 1935 covered terrace; a generic block misses all of it. Clear, square 2021 pano of the Damrak front (w02-134).

targets.name: Café-Restaurant De Kroon (Rembrandtplein 17, 1898, G. van Arkel)
targets.reason: Rembrandtplein north wall, central ride. Gemeentelijk monument 209036: white Jugendstil front with an asymmetric corner tower, glazed first-floor winter garden and balcony, lettered parapet. Drawn today as a generic brick block. Square 2020 pano of the plein front (w02-176) and a 2019 corner view (w05-177).

targets.name: School, Marnixstraat 2 (1883; rijksmonument 518500)
targets.reason: Corner of the Marnixstraat and the Haarlemmerplein side, inner ring. A banded-brick neo-Renaissance school with pointed gabled pavilions, finials and a walled playground with a gate pavilion; generic draws a plain box. Seven usable walls (2018-2024), all fronts clear.
targets.status: next: brief and crops ready (artifacts/landmark-briefs/school-marnixstraat-2/); the pand takes in the walled playground and its gate pavilion, so the 3DBAG shell needs the wall split from the school body

targets.name: Oranjekerk (Van Ostadestraat 149, 1903; gemeentelijk monument 200431)
targets.reason: De Pijp, inner ring (2.3 km). Brick church with a big traceried west window, a tower, an octagonal entrance porch and a parsonage corner; a generic block misrepresents it badly. Very good evidence: 15 walls, most of them clear.

targets.name: Spiegelhof (Nieuwe Spiegelstraat / Herengracht corner, 1905-1917)
targets.reason: High exposure (rank 1 raw, 0.95 km); drawn by the ordinary kit. Stone colonnade along the Nieuwe Spiegelstraat, a curved rusticated stone corner on the Herengracht, a pedimented stone porch. 1507 m2 with several blocks: a large recipe, but evidence is good (10 walls). Next round.

targets.name: Sarphatihuis (Roetersstraat 2, 1779; rijksmonument 4983)
targets.reason: Former Oudemannenhuis on the Nieuwe Herengracht: a 5415 m2 courtyard block with curved wings, a pedimented front and a stone gate. Good evidence, but the size puts it in the large-recipe class.
